title: Autoencoders → MADE
blurb: Why plain autoencoders aren’t generative, and the mask fix

hook.title: Black tape over the future
hook.text: Imagine a student predicting the next word of a sentence from a worksheet. If the worksheet accidentally shows the *answer*, they can copy it. A plain **autoencoder** is that student: given $x$, it reconstructs $x$, and can trivially cheat by copying the input. To turn it into an honest predictor, put **black tape** over everything an output isn't allowed to see: output $i$ may look only at inputs earlier in the ordering. That tape is the **mask** in MADE.
hook.recall: Remember the black tape: MADE’s masks hide the future (and the answer itself) from each output, so the network is a valid autoregressive model and still computes every conditional in a single pass.

explore.intro: Three variables, one hidden layer. Hidden units carry a number $m$; masks follow the slide's rule.
tasks: Choose the slide's ordering $x_2,x_3,x_1$. Is the model valid? Switch to *fully connected*, where do outputs leak?
Click hidden units to change their numbers. Can you break validity while masks are on?
explore.takeaway: Hidden → input connection kept if hidden number $\ge$ input rank; output ← hidden kept if output rank $>$ hidden number (strict). Result: $\hat x_i$ depends only on earlier variables.

build.prompt: Order the construction of MADE masks.
items: Choose an ordering of the variables
Give each hidden unit a random integer in $[1,n-1]$
Connect a hidden unit to inputs whose rank is $\le$ its number
Connect an output to hidden units with a number strictly smaller than its rank
build.explanation: Slide 17: each hidden unit depends on the first $i$ inputs of the ordering; connect to previous-layer units with a smaller or equal number (strictly smaller in the final layer).

questions.prompt: Why is a vanilla autoencoder **not** a generative model?
options: It has no decoder
It doesn’t define a distribution over $x$ that we can sample from
It can’t be trained
It uses too many parameters
questions.explanation: It maps $x\to e(x)\to d(e(x))\approx x$ but there is nothing to sample new $x$ from.

questions.prompt: To make an autoencoder autoregressive (a valid Bayesian network / DAG), what must hold with ordering $x_1,x_2,x_3$?
options: $\hat x_1$ can depend on all inputs
$\hat x_1$ cannot depend on any input and $\hat x_2$ can only depend on $x_1$
$\hat x_2$ can depend on $x_3$
All outputs depend on $x_3$
questions.explanation: No peeking at the answer or the future: only strictly earlier variables.

questions.prompt: MADE on $n=4$ variables: each hidden unit gets a random integer in $[1,n-1]$. How many different values can it take?
Ordering $x_2,x_3,x_1$ (ranks: $x_2{=}1$, $x_3{=}2$, $x_1{=}3$). A hidden unit has number $m=1$. Which outputs may it feed (output rank must be **strictly greater** than $m$)?
options: $\hat x_2$ only
$\hat x_3$ and $\hat x_1$
All three
None
questions.explanation: Ranks of outputs: 1, 2, 3. Strictly greater than 1 gives $\hat x_3$ and $\hat x_1$. That unit sees only $x_2$ (rank ≤ 1).

questions.prompt: In MADE with ordering $x_2,x_3,x_1$, which statement is FALSE?
options: The unit producing $p(x_2)$ cannot depend on any input
The unit for $p(x_3|x_2)$ depends only on $x_2$
One network produces all conditionals in a single pass
The unit for $p(x_2)$ may depend on $x_1$
questions.explanation: $p(x_2)$ is first in the ordering, so it can depend on nothing.

questions.prompt: *“I’ll keep the autoencoder fully connected and just train with log-likelihood; the autoregressive structure will emerge.”* What’s wrong?
options: Nothing
Without masks, output $\hat x_i$ can read $x_i$ (and later variables), so it doesn’t define a valid DAG; the constraint must be built into the architecture
Log-likelihood can’t be used with autoencoders
Fully connected layers can’t be trained
questions.explanation: Tape must be on the paper before the exam, not discovered during it.
